issues.failure_explanation: Lemma 3.1 asserts that $\| sigma^{-1}\|_{\ell_q} \le N < \infty$ holds for any $\eta \in \NN$ for the weights $\sigma_ s$ defined by (3.5). However, along the single-variable subseries $ s = k\mathbf{e}_1$ for $k \ge \eta$, $\sigma_{k\mathbf{e}_1}^2 = \sum_{l=0}^\eta \binom{k}{l} \rho_1^{2l} \le (\eta + 1) k^\eta \max(1, \rho_1^{2\eta})$, which gives $\sigma_{k\mathbf{e}_1}^{-q} \ge C k^{-q\eta/2}$. Whenever $0 < q < 2$ and $\eta \le 2/q$, the exponent satisfies $q\eta/2 \le 1$, and therefore $\sum_{k=1}^\infty \sigma_{k\mathbf{e}_1}^{-q} = \infty$, which directly contradicts $\bsigma^{-1} \in \ell_q(\FF)$. The cited result from BCDM17 guarantees $\ell_q$-summability only when $\eta$ is chosen strictly greater than $2/q$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add the condition $\eta > 2/q$ (or state that there exists $\eta \in \NN$ sufficiently large) to the statement of Lemma 3.1.
issues.overall_effect: In the lognormal case, Lemma 3.1 and Theorem 3.3 fail as stated when $\eta$ is chosen arbitrarily (specifically for any $\eta \le 2/q$).
issues.title: Unrestricted parameter eta causes weight sequence in lognormal case to diverge in ell_q
issues.why_classification: Requiring $\eta > 2/q$ is a standard local condition directly supported by the cited reference BCDM17 that completely resolves the defect without changing the convergence rates or scope of the downstream results in Theorem 3.3.

issues.failure_explanation: Lemma 4.1 claims $\| sigma^{-1}\|_{\ell_q} < \infty$ with $q = p/(1-p)$ for an arbitrary $\eta \in \NN$. However, for $ sigma$ defined by (3.5), the weights on the coordinate ray $ s = k\mathbf{e}_1$ satisfy $\sigma_{k\mathbf{e}_1}^{-q} \ge C k^{-q\eta/2}$. When $p < 2/3$, we have $q < 2$. For any $\eta \le 2/q = 2(1-p)/p$, the sum $\sum_{k=1}^\infty \sigma_{k\mathbf{e}_1}^{-q}$ diverges, so $\bsigma^{-1} \notin \ell_q(\FF)$. The result cited from DNSZ2023 requires $\eta > 2(1-p)/p$. Furthermore, in Theorem 4.2, $\eta$ is left unquantified.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add the hypothesis $\eta > 2(1-p)/p = 2/q$ to Lemma 4.1, and specify that $\eta$ is chosen to satisfy this threshold in Theorem 4.2.
issues.overall_effect: Lemma 4.1 and Theorem 4.2 are invalid as stated whenever $\eta \le 2(1-p)/p$.
issues.title: Unrestricted parameter eta causes weight sequence for holomorphic functions to diverge in ell_q
